issues.legal_issue: The value of multiple rural buildings, each below the applicable individual value threshold, cannot be aggregated to qualify for separate compensation.
material_facts: The displaced claimant had been allotted less than four acres of agricultural land and sought separate compensation for a rural house and shop left behind.
The assessed value of each building was below the applicable individual threshold, although their combined assessed value exceeded it.
The claimant did not settle in the village where agricultural land had been allotted and therefore did not obtain the house or site and building grant available under the alternative arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The value of each rural building had to be considered separately. Because neither building met the applicable threshold, the claimant was not entitled to separate compensation, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under rule 65(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Rules, where less than four acres of agricultural land has been allotted, the assessed value of each rural building must meet the prescribed threshold for separate compensation; rule 65(1) applies the corresponding principle where four or more acres have been allotted. The scheme, read with rule 57, treats lower-value rural buildings as appendages to agricultural property and provides an alternative house or site and building grant. Section 13 of the General Clauses Act, which generally permits singular words to include the plural, does not require aggregation because the context makes the individual building—not its owner’s total holdings—the relevant unit. The Court relied on Makhanlal Malhotra v. Union of India, approved Chanan Das Mukhi v. Union of India, and did not approve Totaram Teckchand v. H. K. Choudhary.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_compensation_order and displaced_person_claims_separate_compensation_for_rural_buildings and allotted_land_fell_in_lower_allotment_category and each_building_below_individual_threshold and combined_building_value_exceeds_threshold

predicates.civil_appeal_from_compensation_order: The matter is a civil appeal challenging an order that granted separate compensation for rural buildings.
predicates.displaced_person_claims_separate_compens: A displaced person seeks separate compensation for rural buildings left behind.
predicates.allotted_land_fell_in_lower_allotment_ca: The displaced person was allotted agricultural land in the category to which the lower individual building-value threshold applies.
predicates.each_building_below_individual_threshold: Each rural building had an assessed value below the individual threshold for separate compensation.
predicates.combined_building_value_exceeds_threshol: The assessed values of the buildings together exceeded the applicable threshold.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a displaced person’s claim for separate compensation for multiple rural buildings, and each building is below the individual threshold despite their combined value exceeding it, eligibility is assessed for each building separately rather than by aggregating their values.
